comment: Every channel's multiplier and divisor are read through the rotation offset (Syncro.cpp:423), so the knob at one row can be driving a different row's output once ROTATE is turned. A channel whose multiplier is 0 holds its upright output at 0V and its inverted output at 10V (Syncro.cpp:483). The tempo is clamped so that the fastest channel stays below the Nyquist frequency, which at 44.1kHz caps the master at about 10336 BPM (Syncro.cpp:329).
